article_title: Expert-led and artificial intelligence (AI) system-assisted tutoring course increase confidence of Chinese medical interns on suturing and ligature skills: prospective pilot study.
citation: Yang Ying-Ying, Shulruf Boaz. (2019). An expert-led and artificial intelligence system-assisted tutoring course to improve the confidence of Chinese medical interns in suturing and ligature skills: a prospective pilot study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2019.16.7
title: WKS-2RII AI suturing assessment and training system (Kyoto-Kagaku)
description: The Waseda-Kyoto-Kagaka suture no. 2 refined II (WKS-2RII; Kyoto-Kagaku) is an AI recording and analysis system connected to artificial skin for suturing/ligature training. "The performance scores of each intern were calculated by comparison (percentage) with the performance of novice learners that had been set as the internal standard in the system." It scores six aspects (time, force in tissue, judging tension, equidistance, distance between sutures, wound dehiscence) mapped to safety, quality, and efficiency domains, returns pass/fail against a total TP threshold of 70, provides reference images and parameters of experts and novices, and served in the study as a self-assessment and training tool supporting self-directed learning and discussion with clinical instructors.
requirements: Interns watch a demonstration video before practicing; a practice session requires 1.5 hours on the system
Scores are discussed with clinical instructors as the basis for feedback
constraints: The article states a total TP score greater than 70 is a passing score and less than 70 a failing score; the system is described as emphasizing safety and quality of suturing/ligature skills
target_learners: Novice medical interns in the surgical block without prior suturing/ligature training
target_learning_goals: Acquisition of suturing and ligature skills (safety, quality, efficiency) and self-assessed confidence performing them on real patients
examples: In the expert-led+AI group, 23 interns practiced on the WKS-2RII after the shared expert-led course, with 13 completing a second and 6 a third session
key_sources: Yang Ying-Ying, Shulruf Boaz. (2019). An expert-led and artificial intelligence system-assisted tutoring course to improve the confidence of Chinese medical interns in suturing and ligature skills: a prospective pilot study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2019.16.7

article_title: Choose Your Own Adventure: Interactive E-Books to Improve Word Knowledge and Comprehension Skills
citation: Stephanie L. Day, Jin K. Hwang, Tracy Arner, Danielle McNamara, Carol M. Connor. (2022). Choose Your Own Adventure: Interactive E-Books to Improve Word Knowledge and Comprehension Skills. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=Choose+Your+Own+Adventure+Interactive+E-Books+Word+Knowledge
title: WKe-Books: interactive choose-your-own-adventure e-books embedding comprehension strategies with immediate feedback
description: The WKe-Books are two interactive digital books, Dragon's Lair (narrative) and Hurricane! (hybrid narrative-informational science text), each delivered in three strategy versions (word learning or general comprehension, summarization, and deep-level question generation). "The WKe-Books were designed to engage young readers through an interactive design using a choose-your-own-adventure and name-your-character format". Multiple-choice questions embedded in each story stream halted progress until answered correctly and provided explicit strategy feedback; Dragon's Lair contained 25 target vocabulary words and Hurricane! taught five target hurricane concepts.
requirements: Classroom reading sessions with 10-minute interventionist-led strategy review sessions before reading
Embedded multiple-choice questions with feedback in each chapter
constraints: Analysis of open-ended embedded question responses was beyond the scope of the feasibility study
Story streams in Dragon's Lair were unbalanced in targeted words and embedded questions
target_learning_goals: Reading comprehension strategy use (summarization, question generation, contextual and morphemic analysis)
examples: Students read Dragon's Lair for 20 minutes per session, three days a week, taking about nine sessions to finish
Hurricane! opened with an embedded short video demonstrating how hurricanes form in the ocean
key_sources: Stephanie L. Day, Jin K. Hwang, Tracy Arner, Danielle McNamara, Carol M. Connor. (2022). Choose Your Own Adventure: Interactive E-Books to Improve Word Knowledge and Comprehension Skills. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=Choose+Your+Own+Adventure+Interactive+E-Books+Word+Knowledge
